simple.meaning: מַלָּח (mallâch) is a Hebrew word meaning “a sailor (as following 'the salt').” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַלָּח (H4419) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezekiel 27:9, with occurrences in Ezekiel, Jonah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַלָּח (H4419) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַלָּח (H4419) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַלָּח (mallâch) / H4419 is traced through Ezekiel 27:9, Ezekiel 27:27, Ezekiel 27:29, Jonah 1:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H4419. mallach [ מַלָּח ] noun masculine mariner (loan-word from Assyrian mala—u Dl HWB 412 compare Id Proverbs 1.178 ; Hal ZA iv. 1880, 53 ; so also Aramaic (see Brock.), whence Arabic Frä 221 ); — plural מַלָּחִים Jonah 1:5 ; Ezek 27:29 ; מַלָּחַיִךְ 27:27 ; מַלָּחֵיהֶם 27:9 (Ba NB 49 Anm. 3 ); — mariners, sailors of ship going to Tarshish Jonah 1:5 (compare הַחֹבֵל רַב 1:6 ); to Tyre Ezek 27:9 , compare 27:27 ; 27:29 (|| חֹבְלִים ). מִלְחָמָה see I. לחם .

occurrences.englishText: Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried to his god. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten the ship. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship, and he was laying down, and was fast asleep.
